{
  /* Deliberately the same strictness as the web client's own tsconfig: this project
     compiles that app's shell and views unchanged, so a stricter setting here
     would report "errors" in code that is correct under the config it is
     written against — and the only fix available would be to edit the web
     client to please the desktop build. Same rules, one source. */
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "lib": ["ES2022", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"],
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "strict": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "types": ["vite/client", "node"],
    /* `paths` is global to the program, which is the point: this project also
       compiles files under packages/ and apps/webapp/, and in the published
       mirror there is no node_modules next to them for a bare "react" to
       resolve into. Pinning the module names here makes `tsc` agree with the
       aliases in vite.config.ts, in both trees. */
    "paths": {
      "react": ["./node_modules/@types/react"],
      "react/jsx-runtime": ["./node_modules/@types/react/jsx-runtime"],
      "react/jsx-dev-runtime": ["./node_modules/@types/react/jsx-dev-runtime"],
      "react-dom": ["./node_modules/@types/react-dom"],
      "react-dom/client": ["./node_modules/@types/react-dom/client"],
      "next-intl": ["./node_modules/use-intl"],
      /* The editor and sanitizer packages, for the same reason as the entries above and
         not for a different one: they are imported from apps/webapp/app/**, and in the
         published mirror there is no node_modules beside those files to walk up into.
         Mapping them here is safe in the monorepo too — TypeScript falls back to ordinary
         module resolution when a `paths` target does not exist, which is what happens in a
         workspace install where the copy lives next to the web client instead. */
      "dompurify": ["./node_modules/dompurify"],
      "parse5": ["./node_modules/parse5"],
      "pdfjs-dist": ["./node_modules/pdfjs-dist"],
      "@tiptap/react": ["./node_modules/@tiptap/react"],
      "@tiptap/starter-kit": ["./node_modules/@tiptap/starter-kit"],
      "@tiptap/extension-link": ["./node_modules/@tiptap/extension-link"],
      "@tiptap/extension-code": ["./node_modules/@tiptap/extension-code"],
      /* The ProseMirror surface under the editor — the line-scoped block commands in
         RichEditor.tsx import `NodeSelection`/`TextSelection` and the position/node types
         from these two subpaths. Same story as `/ics` and `/folder-name` below, third
         verse: in this tree the workspace resolves them through apps/webapp's own
         node_modules and these entries are inert, and in the published mirror they are the
         ONLY resolver — the shared sources live at ../webapp with no node_modules beside
         them, so the walk-up never reaches this project's copy. Their slice declared the
         package in both manifests and missed this map, which failed the mirror's
         `tsc --noEmit` on all three platforms while the monorepo's own gates stayed green.
         The targets are the package's committed proxy dirs (`state/index.ts` re-exporting
         prosemirror-state, likewise `model/`), present in the npm and pnpm layouts alike. */
      "@tiptap/pm/state": ["./node_modules/@tiptap/pm/state"],
      "@tiptap/pm/model": ["./node_modules/@tiptap/pm/model"],
      "@tiptap/pm/transform": ["./node_modules/@tiptap/pm/transform"],
      "@tiptap/pm/view": ["./node_modules/@tiptap/pm/view"],
      "@ohmail/tokens/omarchy-rule": ["../../packages/tokens/omarchy/rule.ts"],
      "@ohmail/tokens/design": ["../../packages/tokens/src/design/tokens.ts"],
      "@ohmail/tokens": ["../../packages/tokens/src/index.ts"],
      "@ohmail/testing/adapter": ["../../packages/testing/src/adapter.ts"],
      "@ohmail/testing": ["../../packages/testing/src/index.ts"],
      /* The durable-write door as a LEAF, and it must be listed BEFORE nothing in particular
         here (TypeScript matches the longest pattern) but it MUST be listed: the published
         mirror has no node_modules beside `packages/app-logic/src/storage/durable.ts`, which re-exports
         this specifier, so this map and `vite.config.ts`'s alias table are its only resolvers.
         Three earlier slices each paid a release CI that died at `tsc --noEmit` on all three
         platforms for exactly this omission; `test/desktop-shell.test.ts` holds both
         entries to each other so there is no fourth. */
      "@ohmail/client-engine/durable": ["../../packages/client-engine/src/durable.ts"],
      "@ohmail/client-engine/send-fingerprint": ["../../packages/client-engine/src/send-fingerprint.ts"],
      "@ohmail/client-engine/html-tree-budget": ["../../packages/client-engine/src/html-tree-budget.ts"],
      "@ohmail/client-engine": ["../../packages/client-engine/src/index.ts"],
      "@ohmail/ui/base": ["../../packages/ui/src/base/index.ts"],
      "@ohmail/ui/mail": ["../../packages/ui/src/mail/index.ts"],
      "@ohmail/ui": ["../../packages/ui/src/index.ts"],
      /* Behaviour without a screen, and the host contract. Same story as the leaves above: in the
         published tree this map and `vite.config.ts`'s alias table are their only resolvers. A
         folder's door resolves as the folder; a moved file by its own name. */
      "@ohmail/app-logic/*": ["../../packages/app-logic/src/*"],
      "@ohmail/app/host/browser": ["../../packages/app/src/host/browser/index.ts"],
      "@ohmail/app/host": ["../../packages/app/src/host/index.ts"],
      "@ohmail/app/keys": ["../../packages/app/src/keys/index.ts"],
      "@ohmail/app/text/fill": ["../../packages/app/src/text/fill.ts"],
      "@ohmail/app/frame/boot": ["../../packages/app/src/frame/boot-stamp.ts"],
      "@ohmail/app/frame": ["../../packages/app/src/frame/index.ts"],
      "@ohmail/app/text": ["../../packages/app/src/text/index.ts"],
      "use-intl/core": ["./node_modules/use-intl/core.d.ts"],
      /* The wire's vocabulary: types only, imported by the client engine and erased at build. This
         install links no workspace package, so this line is what resolves it for `tsc --noEmit`. */
      "@ohmail/wire": ["../../packages/wire/src/index.ts"],
      /* The calendar reader — one of the two `@trafficflow/*` specifiers the desktop program
         compiles, read by the client engine and by the attachment strip and event card. Same
         fallback argument as the dompurify/tiptap block above: in this tree the workspace
         resolves it through `packages/core`'s exports map and this entry is inert, and in the
         published mirror it is the only thing that can resolve it, because there `ics.ts` is a
         lone file with no package.json beside it. */
      "@trafficflow/core/ics": ["../../packages/core/src/ics.ts"],
      "@trafficflow/core/url-escapes": ["../../packages/core/src/url-escapes.ts"],
      "@trafficflow/core/image-dimensions": ["../../packages/core/src/image-dimensions.ts"],
      "@trafficflow/core/away-scope": ["../../packages/core/src/away-scope.ts"],
      /* The organized six and the retro-move question, reached through `@ohmail/client-engine`'s
         re-export — the bundler's twin, and the pair must agree. */
      "@trafficflow/core/destinations": ["../../packages/core/src/destinations.ts"],
      /* The folder-name rules — the second admitted leaf, imported by the shared rail so a
         folder is refused with the server's own sentence BEFORE the wire. Same story as `/ics`
         in both trees: inert here, the only resolver in the mirror. Its slice added the subpath
         to core's exports and missed this map, which failed the mirror's `tsc --noEmit` on all
         three platforms while the monorepo's own gates stayed green — the workspace resolves
         through exports, the mirror only through this list. */
      "@trafficflow/core/folder-name": ["../../packages/core/src/folder-name.ts"],
      /* The mirrors' shared drain policy — the THIRD admitted leaf, imported by the client
         engine so that it and the desktop sidecar's mirror cannot hold two opinions about when
         a local copy is stale, what a surface may say about its age, and how big a catch-up
         page is. Same story as `/ics` and `/folder-name`, and this is the THIRD slice to owe
         this line: the two comments above each record a release CI that died at `tsc --noEmit`
         on all three platforms because the subpath was added to core's exports and not here.
         `test/desktop-shell.test.ts` now holds the two maps to each other
         so there is no fourth. */
      "@trafficflow/core/drain-policy": ["../../packages/core/src/drain-policy.ts"],
      /* `Re: ` exactly once — the FOURTH admitted leaf, and it arrived WITH this line rather than
         owing it. The comment above says the guard "now holds the two maps to each other so there
         is no fourth"; there is a fourth, and the guard is what made it cheap — the map and
         `vite.config.ts`'s alias table are checked against each other, so adding the subpath to
         core's exports and forgetting this list is a red test here instead of a release CI that
         dies at `tsc --noEmit` on all three platforms, which is what the two slices above each
         paid.
         It is imported by `packages/client-engine/src/mutations.ts` and moved out of that file
         because the away responder composes replies too, from `packages/services`, which may not
         import the browser engine. */
      "@trafficflow/core/reply-subject": ["../../packages/core/src/reply-subject.ts"],
      /* The search ranking rule — the FIFTH admitted leaf, and it arrived with this line for the
         reason the fourth did: the guard holds this map and `vite.config.ts`'s alias table to
         each other, so a subpath added to core's exports and forgotten here is a red test rather
         than a release CI that dies at `tsc --noEmit` on all three platforms.
         It is imported by `packages/client-engine/src/search.ts` — the local index — and by
         `packages/services/src/search-service.ts`, which is the whole point: the desktop's own
         search and the hosted archive apply ONE tier rule and one ordering. */
      "@trafficflow/core/search-rank": ["../../packages/core/src/search-rank.ts"],
      /* The pairing link's grammar — the SIXTH admitted leaf, and it arrived with this line for
         the reason the fourth and fifth did. It moved OUT of `packages/client-engine` into core
         because a third graph parses these links now: `apps/sidecar`, whose client door pastes a
         link printed by another machine's desktop and which may not link the client-engine
         barrel. `packages/client-engine/src/pair-link.ts` re-exports it, and that file is in this
         bundle, so the specifier has to resolve here. */
      "@trafficflow/core/pair-link": ["../../packages/core/src/pair-link.ts"],
      "@trafficflow/core/mailto": ["../../packages/core/src/mailto.ts"],
      "@trafficflow/core/sender-headers": ["../../packages/core/src/sender-headers.ts"],
      "@trafficflow/core/rule-order": ["../../packages/core/src/rule-order.ts"],
      "@trafficflow/core/conversation-fold": ["../../packages/core/src/conversation-fold.ts"],
      "@trafficflow/core/reader-refusal": ["../../packages/core/src/reader-refusal.ts"],
      "@trafficflow/core/outbound-text": ["../../packages/core/src/outbound-text.ts"],
      /* The one matcher that decides whether a configured model is on the endpoint's list —
         imported by `AiProviderForm.tsx` and by the engine's Ollama probe, so the picker and
         the verdict cannot disagree. Same story as the leaves above in the mirror. */
      "@trafficflow/core/model-name": ["../../packages/core/src/model-name.ts"],
      /* The diagnostic file's builder, shared with the phone (Settings → About). */
      "@trafficflow/core/diagnostics": ["../../packages/core/src/diagnostics/index.ts"]
    }
  },
  "include": ["src", "../paired-page/src", "vite.config.ts"]
}

  /* Deliberately the same strictness as the web client's own tsconfig: this project
     compiles that app's shell and views unchanged, so a stricter setting here
     would report "errors" in code that is correct under the config it is
     written against — and the only fix available would be to edit the web
     client to please the desktop build. Same rules, one source. */
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "lib": ["ES2022", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"],
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "strict": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "types": ["vite/client", "node"],
    /* `paths` is global to the program, which is the point: this project also
       compiles files under packages/ and apps/webapp/, and in the published
       mirror there is no node_modules next to them for a bare "react" to
       resolve into. Pinning the module names here makes `tsc` agree with the
       aliases in vite.config.ts, in both trees. */
    "paths": {
      "react": ["./node_modules/@types/react"],
      "react/jsx-runtime": ["./node_modules/@types/react/jsx-runtime"],
      "react/jsx-dev-runtime": ["./node_modules/@types/react/jsx-dev-runtime"],
      "react-dom": ["./node_modules/@types/react-dom"],
      "react-dom/client": ["./node_modules/@types/react-dom/client"],
      "next-intl": ["./node_modules/use-intl"],
      /* The editor and sanitizer packages, for the same reason as the entries above and
         not for a different one: they are imported from apps/webapp/app/**, and in the
         published mirror there is no node_modules beside those files to walk up into.
         Mapping them here is safe in the monorepo too — TypeScript falls back to ordinary
         module resolution when a `paths` target does not exist, which is what happens in a
         workspace install where the copy lives next to the web client instead. */
      "dompurify": ["./node_modules/dompurify"],
      "parse5": ["./node_modules/parse5"],
      "pdfjs-dist": ["./node_modules/pdfjs-dist"],
      "@tiptap/react": ["./node_modules/@tiptap/react"],
      "@tiptap/starter-kit": ["./node_modules/@tiptap/starter-kit"],
      "@tiptap/extension-link": ["./node_modules/@tiptap/extension-link"],
      "@tiptap/extension-code": ["./node_modules/@tiptap/extension-code"],
      /* The ProseMirror surface under the editor — the line-scoped block commands in
         RichEditor.tsx import `NodeSelection`/`TextSelection` and the position/node types
         from these two subpaths. Same story as `/ics` and `/folder-name` below, third
         verse: in this tree the workspace resolves them through apps/webapp's own
         node_modules and these entries are inert, and in the published mirror they are the
         ONLY resolver — the shared sources live at ../webapp with no node_modules beside
         them, so the walk-up never reaches this project's copy. Their slice declared the
         package in both manifests and missed this map, which failed the mirror's
         `tsc --noEmit` on all three platforms while the monorepo's own gates stayed green.
         The targets are the package's committed proxy dirs (`state/index.ts` re-exporting
         prosemirror-state, likewise `model/`), present in the npm and pnpm layouts alike. */

      "@tiptap/pm/model": ["./node_modules/@tiptap/pm/model"],
      "@tiptap/pm/transform": ["./node_modules/@tiptap/pm/transform"],

      "@ohmail/testing": ["../../packages/testing/src/index.ts"],
      /* The durable-write door as a LEAF, and it must be listed BEFORE nothing in particular
         here (TypeScript matches the longest pattern) but it MUST be listed: the published
         mirror has no node_modules beside `packages/app-logic/src/storage/durable.ts`, which re-exports
         this specifier, so this map and `vite.config.ts`'s alias table are its only resolvers.
         Three earlier slices each paid a release CI that died at `tsc --noEmit` on all three
         platforms for exactly this omission; `test/desktop-shell.test.ts` holds both
         entries to each other so there is no fourth. */
      "@ohmail/client-engine/durable": ["../../packages/client-engine/src/durable.ts"],
      "@ohmail/client-engine/send-fingerprint": ["../../packages/client-engine/src/send-fingerprint.ts"],
      "@ohmail/client-engine/html-tree-budget": ["../../packages/client-engine/src/html-tree-budget.ts"],

         published tree this map and `vite.config.ts`'s alias table are their only resolvers. A
         folder's door resolves as the folder; a moved file by its own name. */
      "@ohmail/app-logic/*": ["../../packages/app-logic/src/*"],

      "@trafficflow/core/url-escapes": ["../../packages/core/src/url-escapes.ts"],

      "@trafficflow/core/destinations": ["../../packages/core/src/destinations.ts"],
      /* The folder-name rules — the second admitted leaf, imported by the shared rail so a
         folder is refused with the server's own sentence BEFORE the wire. Same story as `/ics`
         in both trees: inert here, the only resolver in the mirror. Its slice added the subpath
         to core's exports and missed this map, which failed the mirror's `tsc --noEmit` on all

      "@trafficflow/core/folder-name": ["../../packages/core/src/folder-name.ts"],

         engine so that it and the desktop sidecar's mirror cannot hold two opinions about when

         page is. Same story as `/ics` and `/folder-name`, and this is the THIRD slice to owe
         this line: the two comments above each record a release CI that died at `tsc --noEmit`

         so there is no fourth. */
      "@trafficflow/core/drain-policy": ["../../packages/core/src/drain-policy.ts"],
      /* `Re: ` exactly once — the FOURTH admitted leaf, and it arrived WITH this line rather than
         owing it. The comment above says the guard "now holds the two maps to each other so there
         is no fourth"; there is a fourth, and the guard is what made it cheap — the map and
         `vite.config.ts`'s alias table are checked against each other, so adding the subpath to
         core's exports and forgetting this list is a red test here instead of a release CI that
         dies at `tsc --noEmit` on all three platforms, which is what the two slices above each

         reason the fourth did: the guard holds this map and `vite.config.ts`'s alias table to
         each other, so a subpath added to core's exports and forgotten here is a red test rather
         than a release CI that dies at `tsc --noEmit` on all three platforms.

      "@trafficflow/core/search-rank": ["../../packages/core/src/search-rank.ts"],
      /* The pairing link's grammar — the SIXTH admitted leaf, and it arrived with this line for
         the reason the fourth and fifth did. It moved OUT of `packages/client-engine` into core

         barrel. `packages/client-engine/src/pair-link.ts` re-exports it, and that file is in this

      "@trafficflow/core/mailto": ["../../packages/core/src/mailto.ts"],
      "@trafficflow/core/sender-headers": ["../../packages/core/src/sender-headers.ts"],
      "@trafficflow/core/rule-order": ["../../packages/core/src/rule-order.ts"],
      "@trafficflow/core/conversation-fold": ["../../packages/core/src/conversation-fold.ts"],
      "@trafficflow/core/reader-refusal": ["../../packages/core/src/reader-refusal.ts"],
      "@trafficflow/core/outbound-text": ["../../packages/core/src/outbound-text.ts"],
      /* The one matcher that decides whether a configured model is on the endpoint's list —
         imported by `AiProviderForm.tsx` and by the engine's Ollama probe, so the picker and
         the verdict cannot disagree. Same story as the leaves above in the mirror. */
      "@trafficflow/core/model-name": ["../../packages/core/src/model-name.ts"],
      /* The diagnostic file's builder, shared with the phone (Settings → About). */
      "@trafficflow/core/diagnostics": ["../../packages/core/src/diagnostics/index.ts"]
    }
  },
  "include": ["src", "../paired-page/src", "vite.config.ts"]
